fixes.explanation: Not quite, because the text doesn't call him that. Matthew 22:35 says he's one of the Pharisees, "…an expert in the law…" The text gives him no priest title at all. Titles are easy to mix up, so no worries, friend.

Yes! Jesus says, "Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind." Then He adds, "This is the first and greatest commandment." The man asked which one is greatest, and Jesus names it plainly. I love a clear answer.

That's a real commandment, one of the ones God gave Israel in Exodus 20:8. But it's not the one Jesus picks here. In Matthew 22:37-38, He says to love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul and mind, and calls that the first and greatest. Good commandment, just not the one Jesus names here.

False, nice work. The two commandments are to love the Lord your God and to love your neighbor as yourself. Jesus says, "All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments." Everything else hangs on them, so they're carrying the weight, not sitting small next to the rest.

David it is. Jesus asks whose son the Christ is, and the Pharisees answer, "David's." David was Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), and in a moment Jesus brings up what David said in the Spirit. Keep that answer in your pocket, because Jesus is about to use it.

Moses, Israel's leader, is a big name (Exodus 3:10), but he's not who they say. When Jesus asks whose son the Christ is, the Pharisees answer, "David's." That's David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3). The answer comes up again in the next question, so remember it.

Aaron was Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), but he's not the answer here. The Pharisees say the Christ is "David's" son. David was Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3). That's the name Jesus builds His next question on.

That's the puzzle. The Pharisees say the Christ is David's son, and then David calls Him "Lord." Jesus asks, "So if David calls Him ‘Lord,’ how can He be David’s son?" Then the text says, "No one was able to answer a word…" (Matthew 22:46).
True. The text says, "No one was able to answer a word…" These were the same Pharisees who gathered together to question Jesus. Now they've got nothing to say.

Yes. The text says, "…from that day on no one dared to question Him any further." The Pharisees had gathered to test Jesus, and now no one dares. Right before that, "No one was able to answer a word…" (Matthew 22:46).

Teaching in the temple courts isn't what the verse mentions. Matthew 22:46 says, "…from that day on no one dared to question Him any further." That's about questioning Him, nothing more. The text doesn't say anything about teaching.
